key_insight: The paper shows that LLMs contain low-overlap, functionally specialized subnetworks that can be updated selectively to reduce catastrophic forgetting in continual learning.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical way to make large models adapt to new tasks with lower compute and memory cost by limiting training and optimizer updates to task-relevant regions.
method: Use gradient-attribution profiling to localize cognition-associated subnetworks.
Route each training example to its corresponding functional subnetwork.
Restrict parameter updates and optimizer states to the selected regions in CiMEO.
evidence_signal: Across 1.4 million sequential instructions, the method reports the best average performance on five generative benchmarks spanning programming, exam-style tasks, and mathematical reasoning.
watch_item: Subnetwork routing depends on accurate functional localization, so misassignment or task drift could weaken performance and complicate deployment.
paper_title: Functional Subnetwork Localization for Efficient Continual Learning in Large Language Models
